name_en: Shimabara guzoni — a hearty New Year's mochi soup cooked and served in its own earthen pot
summary_ja: 丸餅に鶏肉や白菜、根菜、高野豆腐などを土鍋でだしとともに炊き、そのまま食べる具だくさんの雑煮。島原の乱で籠城した天草四郎の一党が兵糧と山海の幸を煮て食したのが始まりと伝わるという。
summary_en: Round mochi, chicken, napa cabbage, root vegetables, and freeze-dried tofu are simmered together in broth in an earthenware pot and served straight from it — a hearty New Year's soup said to trace back to besieged rebels eating provisions and local produce during the Shimabara Rebellion.
source_title: 具雑煮／島原具雑煮 長崎県

name_en: Hikitoshi — a home-raised chicken hot pot thickened with iki-doufu and somen
summary_ja: 自宅で飼っていた鶏をさばいてつくる壱岐の鍋料理で、コクの強い壱州豆腐とかために茹でたそうめんを加えるのが定番という。来客をもてなす奥座敷の鍋がはじまりとされ、「引き通し」が名の由来とされる。
summary_en: Chicken raised at home is butchered for this Iki hot pot, typically enriched with iki-doufu, a rich local tofu, and firm-boiled somen — said to have begun as a dish served to guests in the inner parlor, its name tracing to "hiki-toshi," leading a guest through.
source_title: ひきとおし 長崎県

name_en: Iriyaki — a Tsushima hot pot of home-raised chicken or local fish, its broth finished with soba or somen
summary_ja: 地鶏または近海の魚を椿油で煮た寄せ鍋で、冠婚葬祭でもてなしのためにつくられてきたとされる。具を食べ終えたスープに、対馬特産の対州そばやそうめんを入れて食べるのが地元流という。
summary_en: Home-raised chicken or fresh local fish is simmered in camellia oil for this hot pot, said to have been made for guests at celebrations and services. After the solids are eaten, the broth is traditionally finished with local taishu soba noodles or somen.

name_en: Tsubojiru — a meatless soup of tofu, burdock, and konnyaku served at Buddhist memorial meals
summary_ja: もめん豆腐やごぼう、干ししいたけ、こんにゃくを細かく切り、醤油や塩、砂糖でシンプルに味付けした精進汁。西海市雪浦地区に伝わり、法事の席で出されてきたとされる。盛る椀を坪に見立てて名がついたという。
summary_en: Firm tofu, burdock, dried shiitake, and konnyaku are cut fine and simply seasoned with soy, salt, and sugar into a meatless soup — passed down in Yukiura, Saikai, said to be served at Buddhist memorial meals, its name from the bowl it's served in, likened to a tsubo jar.
